items.stem: A response begins with `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found`. What does this tell the developer?

options.text: The request was valid, but the thing asked for does not exist.
options.feedback: A 4xx code means the request was wrong. A 404 means the named resource is not there.

options.text: The server's code crashed while it was handling the request.
options.feedback: A crash would produce a 5xx code, such as 500.

options.text: The request was malformed, so the server could not read it.
options.feedback: A malformed request would produce a 400 code. In a 404, the request was valid.

options.text: The connection to the server failed before any reply came.
options.feedback: If the connection failed, no response with a status line would have arrived.

items.stem: Select all that apply. A POST request sends the body `{"code":"ITENT 45"}` to the server. Which headers help the server read that body correctly?

options.text: `Content-Type`, which says the body is JSON.
options.feedback: The server needs the format to know how to parse the body.

options.text: `Content-Length`, which says how many bytes of body to read.
options.feedback: Without a length, the server does not know where the body ends.

options.text: `Accept`, which says which formats the client can read back.
options.feedback: `Accept` describes the reply the client wants. It says nothing about the body being sent.

options.text: `Cache-Control`, which sets how long to reuse an answer.
options.feedback: `Cache-Control` appears on responses and controls reuse of answers. It does not describe a request body.

items.stem: In the 201 Created response, where does the server tell the client the address of the new enrollment?

options.feedback: The `Location` header gives the address of the newly created resource so the client can fetch it.
The status line holds the version, the code 201 and the reason Created. It does not hold the address.
`Host` names the website a request is for. It appears in requests, not in this response.
The blank line only marks where the headers end.

items.stem: In the server log you see some lines of text, then an empty line, then `{"code":"ITENT 45"}`. What is the empty line?

options.text: The blank line that ends the headers, with the body below it.
options.feedback: A single empty line separates the headers from the body in every HTTP message.

options.text: The end of the request, so nothing follows the empty line.
options.feedback: The body follows the blank line, so the request continues past it.

options.text: A formatting accident caused by how the terminal prints text.
options.feedback: The blank line is part of the HTTP format and is required.

options.text: The start of a second request sent on the same connection.
options.feedback: A new request would begin with a request line such as `POST /enrollments HTTP/1.1`.
